When the complement system is activated, it produces C3a and C5a. These are both anaphylatoxins which can cause inflammation. C3a causes degranulation of mast cells and basophils. Basophils release histamine which causes the endothelium to become 'leaky' which allows white blood cells to exit the blood vessel. White blood cells can then migrate to the site of infection. C5a is a chemotaxin which attracts neutrophils and macrophages to the site of infection. C3 convertase is an enzyme which cleaves C3 into C3a and C3b. C3b is involved in the process of opsonisation. C3b binds to pathogens to make them more likely to be engulfed by phagocytes. Phagocytes have receptors for C3b and so recognise pathogens more easily. Phagocytosis is one of the functions of neutrophils and macrophages in fighting infection. C3b and C5b combine to form the membrane attack complex which punches holes in the cell membrane of pathogens. This allows the contents of the pathogen to leak out and makes it easier for phagocytes to perform phagocytosis. This was covered in the immune response to viral and bacterial infection tutorial.

The answer is C - 0.77 - this is the sensitivity of the testIn this question you are being asked for the sensitivity of the test.  The sensitivity of a test is the proportion of people with the condition who test positive for it.  So the first thing you need to do is work out how many people actually tested positive.  You are told that 48 out of 180 people have the condition. You are also told that 60 people tested positive. Therefore 12 people who tested positive must not have the condition.  This means that 36 people who had the condition tested positive for it.  So the sensitivity of the test is 36/48 = 0.75  I've also worked out the specificity of the test, just for fun.  The specificity of a test is the proportion of people without the condition who test negative for it.  So first you need to work out how many people don't have the condition.  This is 180-48 = 132 people.  You also know that 12 people tested positive despite not having the condition.  So 12 people tested falsely positive.  This means that 120 people who didn't have the condition tested negative for it.  So the specificity of the test is 120/132 = 0.91

Amnesia is the loss of the ability to recall past events or retain new information. The correct answer is C This is because a pulmonary shunt is when there is blood flow to parts of the alveoli that are not ventilated. This means that the blood passing through the shunt is not exposed to oxygen so it returns to the left side of the heart with an oxygenation status similar to that when it entered. This causes a type of respiratory failure that cannot be treated with oxygen therapy. This is because the oxygen therapy only increases the PO2 in the alveoli, but the blood passing through the shunt is not exposed to the increased PO2. This is a common cause of type 1 respiratory failure. Other causes of type 1 respiratory failure include: Lung disease that impairs gas exchange (e.g. pulmonary oedema, pulmonary fibrosis) and physiological causes of respiratory failure (e.g. pregnancy, sleep apnoea). Type 1 respiratory failure can be treated with oxygen therapy. Type 2 respiratory failure is caused by hypoventilation and can be caused by: Neuromuscular disease (e.g. motor neurone disease, anxiety, obesity), Chest wall deformities (e.g. kyphoscoliosis), Lung disease (e.g. COPD, chest infections), Physiological causes (e.g. sleep apnoea, alcohol intoxication).
